title: Diagnostic and prognostic performance to detect Alzheimer's disease and clinical progression of a novel assay for plasma p-tau217
summary: Head-to-head biomarker paper comparing a novel plasma p-tau217 assay against another p-tau217 measure across diagnostic and prognostic tasks. The focus is primarily assay comparison and biomarker-performance characterization, making it closer to methods than to a pure clinical cohort outcome study.
full_text: Background and objective: determine the clinical performance of a novel plasma p-tau217 assay and perform a head-to-head comparison against an established plasma p-tau217 assay in two independent cohorts. Methods: one cohort compared controls and MCI, and another longitudinal MCI cohort was followed for conversion to AD dementia; both assays were evaluated against amyloid status, cognition, and prognosis. Conclusion: the new assay showed diagnostic and prognostic performance similar to the established assay, with good agreement between platforms.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the paper's primary contribution is head-to-head benchmarking of a novel p-tau217 assay against an established assay, even though it reports diagnostic and prognostic endpoints.

title: Performance of a fully-automated Lumipulse plasma phospho-tau181 assay for Alzheimer's disease
summary: Assay-performance paper evaluating a high-throughput fully automated Lumipulse plasma p-tau181 platform across participants spanning the Alzheimer continuum. Although it reports diagnostic and prognostic ability, the center of gravity is the behavior of a specific assay platform and its readiness for scalable routine testing.
full_text: Design: plasma from clinically unimpaired older adults, MCI, and AD dementia participants was analyzed with a fully automated Lumipulse p-tau181 platform and related to CSF amyloid status, PET, MRI, and longitudinal cognition. The paper emphasizes analytic behavior of the automated platform, threshold behavior, and how the platform performs across established Alzheimer biomarker readouts. Conclusion: the automated assay captures AD-related signal and is positioned as a scalable blood-testing platform for routine implementation.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled methods because the main novelty is performance characterization of a specific fully automated Lumipulse platform and its readiness for scalable routine deployment.

title: Clinical value of plasma pTau181 to predict Alzheimer's disease pathology in a large real-world cohort of a memory clinic
summary: Real-world memory-clinic study testing whether plasma pTau181 can screen for Alzheimer pathology and predict conversion from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer dementia. The paper emphasizes clinical applicability, context of use, and prognostic utility in routine patients rather than technical assay construction.
full_text: Setting and cohort: consecutive memory-clinic patients underwent plasma pTau181 testing with reference pathology information available in a substantial subset. The analysis asks whether plasma pTau181 can help predict underlying AD pathology and clinical progression in a real-world diagnostic pathway, including patients with subjective cognitive decline and MCI. Interpretation: the biomarker is framed as a clinical decision-support tool for triage and prognosis in routine care rather than as a platform-development paper.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled clinical because the contribution is real-world decision support and prognostic use in a memory clinic, not development or comparison of a biomarker platform.

title: Validity and Performance of Blood Biomarkers for Alzheimer Disease to Predict Dementia Risk in a Large Clinic-Based Cohort
summary: Prospective multicenter memory-clinic cohort study evaluating whether baseline plasma Aβ42/40, total tau, p181-tau, and NfL improve 5-year prediction of Alzheimer or mixed dementia in patients with subjective cognitive complaints or mild cognitive impairment. The paper focuses on clinical utility and prognostic performance in a real patient cohort rather than analytical assay development.
full_text: Methods and framing: patients from memory-clinic settings were followed longitudinally to test whether baseline blood biomarkers improve prediction of future Alzheimer or mixed dementia beyond routine clinical information. The emphasis is not assay optimization but practical prediction of dementia risk over five years in a clinic-based population. Conclusion: blood biomarkers are evaluated as prognostic tools for real patient management and risk stratification.
gold_slot_rationale: Labeled clinical because the main claim is prognostic and screening usefulness in routine memory-clinic patients, not optimization of a new assay platform.
